title: 'I Don't Understand If It's Such a Big Issue': Shuhei Yoshida Isn't Too Bothered About No More Discs
author: Push Square; Stephen Tailby
content:
He adds that physical and special editions of games will likely still be released, so those who want something tangible will probably be able to buy them at retail — they'll just contain a PS Store code rather than a disc.
As far as Yoshida is concerned, however, the disc itself is fast becoming redundant in the digital age.
"Even with physical disc games, in most cases, developers are constantly updating and adding game data anyway. Anyone who chooses to purchase a physical version will still need to download new patches, DLC, or updates. So, not having a disc, I don't understand if it’s such a big issue."
It's a fair point, though not completely accurate. Many games you can buy on disc do not in fact require any updates, and will work as soon as you slot them into your console.
Obviously, that's not the case for every game; some do necessitate an online connection, while others are incomplete or perhaps even not on the disc at all, requiring a download to play.
The issue isn't straightforward, and Yoshida's thoughts don't account for everything; there's the small matter of digital games never truly belonging to you, for example.
Anyway, it's always interesting to hear his perspective as someone who's been in the business for such a long time.
summary: Shuhei Yoshida believes that physical discs are becoming redundant in the digital age because modern games frequently require downloads, patches, and updates regardless of format. He notes that physical and special editions will likely survive by containing digital store codes instead of discs for those who want tangible items. However, some games can still be played directly from a disc without updates, and digital purchases raise concerns about true ownership.
key_points: Shuhei Yoshida views physical game discs as increasingly redundant.
Physical editions may transition to offering digital store codes.
Many modern physical games still require downloads, patches, and updates.
Some physical games can be played immediately without any updates.
Digital game purchases do not grant the same sense of ownership as physical items.

title: Framework Claims Up To 70% Increase In Battery Life As It Transitions To Intel Wildcat Lake For Laptop 12
author: Sarfraz Khan
content:
The company has switched to the newer Intel Core Series 3 processors for superior battery life, starting at just $549.
Framework Laptop 12 Gets New Configurations With Intel Core Series 3 Wildcat Lake Processors, Starting at $549
Popular laptop manufacturer Framework has introduced its latest Laptop 12 series, featuring the Intel Core Series 3 processors. This series transitions from Intel 13th-gen SKUs to the latest Wildcat Lake processors, aiming at the affordable market while also delivering a power-efficient and lightweight experience.
The company says that they have also added Thunderbolt 4, WiFi 7, and features such as a fingerprint reader and a backlit keyboard. Also, this is the first time a pre-built version is preloaded with Fedora Linux for customers. The pre-orders have been opened and the first batch (Batch 1) will start shipping in October.
![A range of Framework Laptop 12 models are displayed in various modes, including a 2-in-1 design with 'Configure now' text and features like Linux support and Intel Core Series 3 processors.](https://cdn.wccftech.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Laptop-12-configuration-2.jpg)
The Framework 12 is an existing laptop lineup that featured processors like Intel Core i5 1334U, but now the new laptop configurations will include SKUs such as the Core 3 304, Core 5 320, and Core 7 350. The Core 3 304 is the base configuration, featuring a 1+4 core configuration and up to 4.3 GHz, while the Core 5 320 and Core 7 350 will boast a 2+4 core configuration with up to 4.6-4.8 GHz.
With the change in the SKUs, users will receive either one Xe3-based iGPU or two Xe3 GPU cores if they opt for the Core 5 or Core 7 SKU. In any case, Framework promises high power efficiency for improved battery life, low noise, and better surface temperatures. The company says it has found that the Core 5 320-based Laptop 12 delivers a staggering 70% increase in battery life when streaming Netflix 4K content compared to the Core i5 1334U.
![](https://cdn.wccftech.com/files/placeholder-desktop.png) 
![A pair of hands is performing assembly on a Framework laptop, available with Intel Core processors, with specifications for Core 3 304, Core 5 320, and Core 7 350 listed on the side.](https://cdn.wccftech.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Framework-Laptop-12-configuration.jpg)
As far as connectivity is concerned, the Laptop 12 brings two expansion card slots that support Thunderbolt 4 for faster devices. The configuration can support up to 64 GB of DDR5-5600 memory and up to 2 TB of M.2 2230 storage. The price starts at $549, but when you add a single 8 GB DDR5 memory stick and a 500 GB SSD, the price reaches $844. By adding more memory and storage, the price will easily go past $1000, and will further increase as users add a dedicated OS, expansion cards, or customize the keyboard.
News Source: Framework
Follow Wccftech on Google to get more of our news coverage in your feeds.
summary: Framework has introduced its updated Laptop 12 series featuring Intel Core Series 3 processors, starting at $549. The new models transition from older 13th-gen SKUs to Wildcat Lake processors, delivering up to a 70% increase in battery life. Additional updates include Thunderbolt 4 support, WiFi 7, and a pre-built Fedora Linux option, with Batch 1 shipping in October.
key_points: Framework Laptop 12 configurations now feature Intel Core Series 3 (Wildcat Lake) processors starting at $549.
The new Core 5 320 configuration claims up to a 70% increase in battery life during 4K Netflix streaming compared to the previous Core i5 1334U model.
New features include Thunderbolt 4 support, WiFi 7, a fingerprint reader, a backlit keyboard, and a pre-built version preloaded with Fedora Linux.
Pre-orders are currently open, with the first batch scheduled to begin shipping in October.

title: We tested the Pixel 11's Tensor G6 chip, and the results are brutal
author: Robert Triggs
content:
We tested the Pixel 11's Tensor G6 chip, and the results are brutal
Aug 20, 2026 — 5:00 AM ET
![google tensor g6 hero pixel 11 pro xl 5 Photo of a Tensor G6 chip render displayed on a Pixel 11 Pro XL.](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/google-tensor-g6-hero-pixel-11-pro-xl-5-scaled.jpg)
I’ll be frank, my hopes for the Tensor G6 were mixed coming into the launch of the Pixel 11 series. Google has made meaningful upgrades to the CPU and TPU for traditional app and AI workloads, respectively, while switching to what should be a more efficient modem. But pairing the Pixel 11 Pro with just 12GB of RAM, down from 16GB last year, undermines its high-end AI credentials. Meanwhile, Google has dropped a CPU core from its configuration, reducing the benefits of its more modern architecture.
While we can’t blame Google for the current state of the global RAM supply chain, its decision to switch to yet another mid-range graphics chip is harder to defend. Still, now that we have the phone in hand (and managed to get around Google blocking benchmarks via the Play Store), we’ve been able to run our usual suite of benchmarks to get a feel for where the Pixel 11 series falls in the performance pecking order.
The results aren’t great.
What do you think of Google's Tensor G6 approach?
Yearly improvements, but the pace is too slow
|  | Google Tensor G6 | Google Tensor G5 | Google Tensor G4 | Google Tensor G3 | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CPU | Google Tensor G6 1x Arm C1-Ultra (4.11GHz) 4x Arm C1-Pro (3.38GHz) 2x Arm C1-Pro (2.65GHz)  | Google Tensor G5 1x Arm Cortex-X4 (3.78GHz) 5x Arm Cortex-A725 (3.05GHz) 2x Arm Cortex-A520 (2.25GHz)  | Google Tensor G4 1x Arm Cortex-X4 (3.1GHz) 3x Arm Cortex-A720 (2.6GHz) 4x Arm Cortex-A520 (1.92GHz)  | Google Tensor G3 1x Arm Cortex-X3 (2.91GHz) 4x Arm Cortex-A715 (2.37GHz) 4x Arm Cortex-A510 (1.70GHz)  | 
| GPU | Google Tensor G6 PowerVR CXTP-48-1536 (1.29GHz) | Google Tensor G5 PowerVR DXT-48-1536 (1.1GHz) | Google Tensor G4 Arm Mali-G715 (MC7?) (940MHz)  | Google Tensor G3 Arm Mali-G715 MC7 (890MHz)  | 
| RAM | Google Tensor G6 LPDDR5X | Google Tensor G5 LPDDR5X | Google Tensor G4 LPDDR5X | Google Tensor G3 LPDDR5X | 
| Machine Learning | Google Tensor G6 Fifth-gen Tensor Processing Unit | Google Tensor G5 Fourth-gen Tensor Processing Unit | Google Tensor G4 Third-gen Tensor Processing Unit | Google Tensor G3 Third-gen Tensor Processing Unit | 
| Security Co-processor | Google Tensor G6 Titan M3 | Google Tensor G5 Titan M2 | Google Tensor G4 Titan M2 | Google Tensor G3 Titan M2 | 
| Modem | Google Tensor G6 MediaTek M90 | Google Tensor G5 Samsung Exnos | Google Tensor G4 Samsung Exnos | Google Tensor G3 Samsung Exnos | 
| Process | Google Tensor G6 TSMC 3nm | Google Tensor G5 TSMC 3nm | Google Tensor G4 Samsung 4nm | Google Tensor G3 Samsung 4nm | 
To start our dive into the new Tensor G6, let’s look at performance over the last few years to help frame how the Pixel series has improved. Starting on the CPU side, the Tensor G6 moves up to an Arm C1-Ultra at 4.11GHz for the big core, four Arm C1-Pro cores at 3.38GHz for multitasking power, and two Arm C1-Pro cores at 2.65GHz for energy efficiency. While that’s one less core than last year, the Tensor G6 has skipped ahead two CPU generations this time, which, in theory, should lead to a rather significant performance jump compared to the Tensor G5. Unfortunately, the benchmark results are more of a mixed bag.
According to Geekbench 6, single-core performance is up by around 18%, and multi-core performance gains are in the region of 21%. That’s an undoubtedly welcome boost and a very promising generational gain. The chip is certainly fast enough to ensure the Pixel 11 series feels very responsive for everyday and even more demanding tasks. However, if you were hoping for performance approaching that of Samsung’s Exynos 2600, you may be disappointed.
The Exynos uses similar CPU cores at even more conservative clock speeds, yet its larger core count gives it a substantial advantage. My Galaxy S26 Plus scores 18% and 51% higher in single- and multi-core tests, respectively, than the Pixel 11 Pro XL. There are a couple of possible explanations for Google’s performance deficit: more aggressive thermal management, or perhaps smaller cache sizes. We know Arm’s powerhouse cores love big caches, but Google appears to be trying to save as much silicon area as possible.
But it’s the graphics situation that reveals Google’s stark lack of progress in one of mobile’s most popular commuting use cases. According to 3DMark’s Wild Life and Wild Life Extreme tests, peak performance has increased by about 7% to 10% compared to last year’s processor, depending on the exact test. Again, that’s a welcome boost and could be enough to turn somewhat wobbly frame rates into a mostly locked 60 fps. But it isn’t enough to transform the Pixel 11 into a top-performing gaming phone capable of sustaining 120 fps in the latest titles.
CPU, GPU, and TPU performance are up year-on-year.
Unfortunately, that’s about as good as the news gets for prospective Pixel gamers. Looking at the stress-test results suggests that over longer gaming sessions, particularly in warm climates, there may not be much to tell between the Pixel 11 and Pixel 10 series after just a few minutes of intensive gameplay. Performance actually dips to below last year’s GPU after just a few minutes of 3DMark’s stress test, indicating that those higher GPU clocks aren’t particularly sustainable in the long term. Still, real games often take longer to heat up a handset, and we see rival flagships drop performance far more quickly.
Rival flagships offer far more performance
![google pixel 11 pro xl geekbench 6 VS google pixel 11 pro xl geekbench 6 VS](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/google-pixel-11-pro-xl-geekbench-6-VS.jpg)
The real problem is that Google’s latest gains haven’t meaningfully closed the gap. Snapdragon-powered rivals retain a colossal 37% single-core and 52% multi-core advantage over the Pixel 11, and the next Snapdragon refresh is just a few months away. Likewise, Apple’s custom CPU cores offer a hefty 44% advantage in this test, while the deca-core Samsung Exynos 2600 smashes ahead to a 50% multi-core lead.
Google’s Tensor G6 is plenty powerful for daily tasks; its CPU setup scores about as well as the 2025-era Dimensity 9400, which is a very potent chip. However, CPU performance remains a very important metric, despite the increasing focus on features like AI and gaming. Not only does a powerhouse CPU ensure that apps launch quickly, videos encode promptly, and games run smoothly, but its main cores also serve as an important backup for running AI tasks that don’t yet tap into Google’s proprietary TPU hardware. As rival CPUs become faster while adding their own SME2-class AI acceleration, Google’s decision to prioritize TPU performance at the expense of CPU and GPU muscle starts to look increasingly difficult to justify.
For gamers, Google’s AI-first strategy leaves the Pixel playing in the second league for another year.
![google pixel 11 pro xl 3dmark wild life extreme stress test VS google pixel 11 pro xl 3dmark wild life extreme stress test VS](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/google-pixel-11-pro-xl-3dmark-wild-life-extreme-stress-test-VS.jpg)
In terms of peak performance, the Tensor G6’s PowerVR CXT graphics setup is easily bested. The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5’s Adreno 840 produces more than double the score in 3DMark’s Wild Life Extreme test, as does the Arm G1-Ultra inside the Dimensity 9500 (+135% versus Tensor). Apple’s own silicon has a 60% advantage in this test, and the AMD Xclipse 940 in Samsung’s Exynos also bests Tensor by a notable 90%, almost doubling its peak performance. In other words, rival flagship phones selling for a comparable price can often offer more than double the frame rate or let you play games with far higher graphics settings than the Pixel 11.
Rivals more than double Tensor's graphics capabilities.
If there’s a silver lining for the Tensor G6, it’s that its stress-test performance means it gives up far less of its peak potential than these faster competitors. Google’s chip retains about 79% of its peak potential at the end of a 20-run stress test, compared to results ranging from 75% to just 50% for its rivals. However, other chipsets are so far ahead in raw performance that even significant temperature buildup and gameplay times leave them comfortably ahead of Google’s latest silicon, even under the worst conditions.
In addition, there’s still no ray-tracing support in the Tensor G6. While still not a mainstream mobile gaming technology, an increasing number of games are using it. The fact that other silicon vendors are now in their third or fourth generation of capable hardware, with Google not making a move of its own, highlights where its priorities lie.
What is Tensor for?
Google’s vision for Tensor has always extended beyond traditional performance metrics. The fact that the company has focused on boosting TPU performance for on-device AI capabilities by a significant 50% this year, while CPU and GPU see just a fraction of that performance uplift, only serves to reinforce the point that Google is fully on board with the belief that new AI features will keep driving Pixel sales. Everyone else can fight it out for legacy benchmark titles as far as it’s concerned.
Fair enough. But it’s tough to ignore just how far behind Google is falling. Whether Google believes it or not, that has repercussions for a significant number of consumers. As discussed, CPU performance remains the backbone of increasingly demanding mobile experiences, from heavy content creation to PC-class capabilities. Likewise, gaming is a well-trodden mobile pastime that’s more popular than ever, and a good portion of consumers expect their increasingly expensive flagship phones to play the latest games and emulated classics at buttery-smooth frame rates.
![google tensor g6 hero pixel 11 pro xl 1 Photo of a Tensor G6 chip render displayed on a Pixel 11 Pro XL.](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/google-tensor-g6-hero-pixel-11-pro-xl-1-scaled.jpg)
There’s also futureproofing to consider. Google markets its handsets with seven-year lifespans yet ships phones with performance that’s easily a year, if not two, behind what rivals offer. Even Google’s own rate of change in the AI department has left previous-generation phones without some of its latest and greatest features, leaving us to question whether jumping into Pixel for the chip’s TPU prowess is really all that justifiable in the first place. Combined with this year’s RAM downgrade, Google’s AI-first pitch becomes difficult to square with the Pixel 11’s long-term prospects.
Perhaps the Tensor G6 offers a significant improvement in battery life that will put it in a favorable light; we’ll be testing that soon enough. But in the meantime, this year’s Tensor G6 deep dive leads to the same conclusion as the past few years: buy a Pixel 11 if you love Google’s unique features, but it might be best to skip it if you want the best performance money can buy.
summary: The Pixel 11's new Tensor G6 chip delivers modest generational improvements in CPU and GPU performance, but it still falls significantly behind rival flagship processors from Snapdragon, Apple, and Samsung. Google has instead chosen to prioritize its fifth-generation TPU for AI workloads, while reducing the device's RAM and omitting ray-tracing support. Consequently, while the phone is responsive for daily tasks, it lags behind competitors in raw performance and long-term gaming capabilities.
key_points: Geekbench 6 tests show single-core and multi-core CPU performance improvements of roughly 18% and 21%, respectively, but rivals maintain a massive performance advantage.
Graphics performance sees a modest 7% to 10% peak increase, but sustained GPU stress tests show performance can dip below last year's model after a few minutes of intensive gameplay.
Google has focused its strategy on boosting TPU performance for on-device AI by roughly 50%, at the expense of CPU and GPU muscle.
The Tensor G6 lacks ray-tracing support, and the Pixel 11 features a RAM downgrade to 12GB compared to 16GB on the previous model.

title: Pixel Watch 1 not losing Google Health sleep, workout support
author: Abner Li
content:
![google pixel watch](https://9to5google.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2023/02/Pixel-Watch-Concentric-1.jpg?quality=82&strip=all&w=1600) 
On Tuesday, Pixel Watch 1 owners encountered a Google Health error message about needing to update their wearable. Google has confirmed that this was a bug and that the original device remains supported.
The following error message appeared for some Pixel Watch 1 owners in the Google Health app:
Update your watch to keep using Google Health
Your watch is running an older version of Wear OS and will soon stop syncing sleep and workout data with Google Health. Update your watch to the latest version to keep tracking your health.
Google rolled out the last Pixel Watch 1 update in October 2025. This was Wear OS 5.1 based on Android 15 with a June 5, 2025 security patch.
During its lifetime, the wearable ran Wear OS 3.5 (Android 11), Wear OS 4 (Android 13), Wear OS 5 (Android 14), and Wear OS 5.1 (Android 15). The Pixel Watch was guaranteed three years of updates.
In a forum post this afternoon, Google said the “Pixel Watch 1 remains fully supported” and that there was a “bug where some users received this card incorrectly.”

The device received its final update, Wear OS 5.1, in October 2025 as part of its three-year update guarantee.
key_points: Pixel Watch 1 users saw an error message in the Google Health app about losing sync support.
Google confirmed the error message was the result of a bug.
The Pixel Watch 1 remains fully supported by Google.
The device received its final update, Wear OS 5.1 based on Android 15, in October 2025.

title: HP's Googlebook leak highlights support for 'Continue On,' Google's version of Handoff
author: Tushar Mehta
content:
HP's Googlebook leak highlights support for 'Continue On,' Google's version of Handoff
Aug 19, 2026 — 3:57 AM ET
- After Lenovo’s leak, we’re getting a glimpse of HP’s upcoming Googlebook.
- While HP’s leaked Googlebook doesn’t reveal much, it confirms a key software functionality called “Continue On.”
- Continue On is Google’s analog for Apple-style Handoff between different devices, and is making its first appearance in relation to Googlebooks.
Google is reportedly preparing to reveal its first crop of Googlebook-labeled devices next month. Google won’t manufacture them itself, but will instead rely on other popular laptop brands. HP is expected to be one of these brands associated with making new successors to Chromebooks, and a recent leak shares the first look at one of HP’s upcoming offerings.
Leaker Evan Blass has shared on X a glimpse of the upcoming HP Googlebookfollows previous leaks of similar devices from other brands, including Acer, ASUS, and Lenovo.
![hp googlebook hp googlebook](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hp-googlebook.jpeg)
The leak only shows the laptop’s screen, featuring Gmail in a two-pane layout similar to what we see on book-style foldables and tablets. On the taskbar, we also see an additional Chrome icon with a tiny phone on it, suggesting Googlebooks could support Apple-style Handoff functionality for web browsing and other supported use cases. The feature has already been previewed as “Continue On,” and could finally make its official debut with Googlebook devices, expected to launch next month. That said, it’s also vital to note that the screenshot appears a bit warped, which puts a dent in our confidence about Continue On actually making its way to Googlebooks.
The leak doesn’t reveal many details about HP’s hardware, unlike previous highly revealing leaks for devices of other brands. Blass doesn’t shed any light on aspects such as the display size, the keyboard, or touchscreen support on the device. The image hints at a dark blue or bluish-gray color for the outer shell and top case, along with a physical shutter for the webcam. The laptop doesn’t seem to have a detachable form factor, though it might support 360º rotation along the hinge.
Based on early leaks, Googlebooks are expected to come with a variety of chips from Intel, Qualcomm, or MediaTek. Blass doesn’t reveal that either, so we’ll have to wait for details to emerge during or ahead of the launch.
summary: A recent leak of an upcoming HP Googlebook shared by Evan Blass highlights a new software feature called 'Continue On,' Google's version of Apple's Handoff. Expected to debut on Googlebook devices launching next month, the feature is hinted at by a taskbar icon showing a Chrome logo with a tiny phone. While the leak reveals little about HP's hardware aside from color and a webcam shutter, similar devices are anticipated from brands like Acer, ASUS, and Lenovo.
key_points: A leaked image of an HP Googlebook reveals a new software feature named 'Continue On,' similar to Apple's Handoff.
The feature is suggested by a taskbar icon featuring a Chrome logo with a small phone.
Google is expected to reveal its first Googlebook-labeled devices next month, manufactured by brands like HP, Acer, ASUS, and Lenovo.
The leaked image also hints at a dark blue or bluish-gray shell color and a physical webcam shutter, though hardware details remain scarce.

What To Expect In Chapter 7, Season 4 ‘Override’
First off, here’s the new Battle Pass:
The lineup includes K1TTYW1NS, Phantom, Grace Crowne, Geno, Sonic the Hedgehog, Mali, Wrixel, and Bastian. Phantom and Bastian are both very cool. I also like Grace Crowne and Mali.
Map Changes:
The Island has been “hacked” and partially rebooted around a giant central Spire. The expected new locations are:
- Geno’s HQ
- Green Hill Zone
- The Spire
- Temple
- Pac-Man Island
Green Hill Zone is the most substantial crossover location shown so far, bringing actual Sonic loops, rings and checkerboard terrain to the battle royale map. Calamari Canyon, Frosted Flats and Sinister Strip are reportedly leaving, while the rest of the Chapter 7 map largely should remain roughly unchanged.
New Gameplay:
The most interesting additions shown or strongly indicated are:
- Sonic Spin Dash Mythic: High-speed traversal that can run up walls and around Green Hill loops. You know, like how Sonic moves.
- Mega Man Mythic: An arm cannon with a chargeable attack.
- Tetrimino Junk Rift: Drops giant Tetris blocks onto an area, which could interact in interesting ways with a game at least partially about building.
- 8-Bit Shotgun: A pixelated close-range weapon which reminds me of the DOOM pixel shotgun that was released in Call of Duty a couple years ago.
- Masamune AR and Shingen SMG: Futuristic weapons shown being dual-wielded.
- New Sprites: Sonic, Tails, Jazz Jackrabbit, Klombo and several original Sprites. Tails appears to provide aerial mobility, while Sonic provides speed.
- Cartridge system: Players apparently insert cartridges into the Island’s central system, triggering match-wide modifiers that affect everybody—not merely the squad activating them.
It’ll be interesting to see what exactly these cartridges do and what kind of modifiers are added to a match, as this could genuinely impact the game in fun (or infuriating) ways.
The Story So Far
I admit, I’m behind on my Fortnite lore and don’t pay that much attention to the story beats as this is much more of a casual interest for me these days. But the story leading into Season 4 is basically more Zero Point shenanigans.
During the August 15 “Unstable” Story Moment, Doctor Slone attempted to stabilize the damaged Zero Point. Geno hacked the stabilizer, overwhelmed Slone’s controls and stole the Zero Point, leaving a game cartridge in its place. The new season’s premise is to override Geno’s system and take back the Island. But to what end? We’ll all still be stuck on the island forever, killing one another like some crazed Gilligan’s Island parody. (Now there’s a crossover for you, Epic Games).
Get your challenges done fast, young padawans. Fortnite will be down in a matter of hours.

title: I spent a week testing the Google Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL, and they're harder to recommend despite some fun new Gemini features
author: Nicholas Sutrich
content:
Android Central Verdict
The Google Pixel 11 Pro family gives you a true choice of size without any compromise between the models. Camera hardware improvements are notable over the Pixel 10 Pro, and Magic Capture is one of the best camera features I've used on any phone to date. New Gemini features like Rambler are truly wonderful additions to the Android experience, and several other standout features mark a solid software release. But Pixel phones have been too expensive lately, and this year's $100+ price increase makes that worse. With less RAM than last year, a GPU that still doesn't support the latest Vulkan APIs, and a poor PWM rate on the display, this one's hard to recommend.
Pros
- +True choice of sizes without compromise
- +Magic Capture might be the best camera feature ever
- +Camera improvements are solid
- +Very bright displays
- +Impressively solid new Gemini features (like Rambler)
Cons
- -More expensive
- -Less RAM
- -Poor PWM rate
- -GPU still doesn't support the latest Vulkan APIs
- -Smaller batteries and slower charging than Pixel 10
Why you can trust Android Central
Every year, buying a Pixel feels a little bit like making a deal with Darth Vader. What started as an incredible-sounding concept slowly became less desirable. Even when something gets better, something else seems to get worse. I can almost hear Google telling me to pray it doesn't alter the deal any further.
Case in point: the Google Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL. This year, you'll get less base RAM, a slightly smaller battery, and a GPU that's still not particularly capable. But you'll also get amazing new features like Magic Capture, Creator suite, instant Night Sight, live translation for videos, and the new Rambler voice keyboard.
Are those enough to make us forget about these devices' shortcomings? In some ways, absolutely, as Pixels are designed to appeal to the masses (who often don't care as much about raw performance or other metrics), and we were initially impressed with many of the new Gemini features arriving on the Pixel 11 series during our hands-on.
However, a year with the Pixel 10 Pro and more time with the Pixel 11 Pro have shown me that Google is more focused on figuring out its next big AI toy than on putting good work into creating truly great phones.
Starting off on the wrong foot
 ![The back of the olive green Google Pixel 11 Pro XL](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/SHQKoFFu7jFKMsDvg7mGta.jpg) 
Last year, Google removed the physical SIM tray in U.S. models, and this year brings about its own reductions. The entry Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL models ship with 12GB of RAM to start, 4GB less than last year, and the XL is $100 more than last year on top of that. RAMageddon is certainly causing problems Google can't control, but it still feels bad to get something worse for a higher price.
Both models feature smaller batteries and, somehow, slower charging, despite claiming otherwise. Data from our parent company's Future Labs backs up this claim (see below). Google also no longer includes a year of Gemini Pro with these phones, instead giving just six months of the service to Pixel owners.
| Pixel 11 vs. Pixel 10 charging speed |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Charging | Pixel 10 Pro | Pixel 11 Pro | Pixel 10 Pro XL | Pixel 11 Pro XL | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15-minute charge (45W) | 27% | 27% | 33% | 27% | 
| 30-minute charge (45W) | 55% | 51% | 63% | 54% | 
And while Tensor G6 is supposed to be a bit more efficient, our battery tests show near-identical battery life between equivalent Pixel 10 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro models. Tensor G6 is most certainly faster than the G5 in many areas, but overall performance still puts this chip several years behind the competition.
Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android
To make matters worse, while the PowerVR GPU here performs better than the one in the Pixel 10, it still doesn't support the latest Vulkan API, meaning games that require Vulkan for advanced performance or graphics (like Minecraft's Vibrant Visuals setting) will give you worse visuals on a Pixel 11 Pro series phone. This is particularly disappointing because this year's GPU performs much better than last year's.
 ![Playing Minecraft on a Google Pixel 11 Pro XL](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/P7s5VXurCm3b3NxKmHS3XM.jpg) 
I also can't say I've found better cell coverage on these phones despite the change in modem. My calls get dropped in the same areas as the Pixel 10, while phones from Motorola and Honor (for example) hang on to the signal without issue.
And, of course, there's the display. Google loves to highlight how color-accurate and insanely bright its displays are, but the company's use of low-frequency PWM dimming continues to make its phones unusable for flicker-sensitive people year after year.
None of these things would be quite as egregious if Google weren't charging as much as Samsung or Apple, but the reality is that these are too expensive for what you get.
Experience over performance
 ![The Pixel Tips app on a Google Pixel 11 Pro XL](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/heyY69Wd5XWQRt3R9wTBGS.jpg) 
Pixel has long focused on delivering a unique experience that trumps raw performance, and most of the new features fit that mantra. Magic Capture, a new camera mode that automatically takes pictures for you, feels like the first time the term "Magic" was correctly applied to one of Google's Gemini experiments.
It's an upgraded version of what Honor introduced two and a half years ago, and it feels truly magical to use. Open the camera, select Magic Capture, tap start, and you'll soon have a video plus truly amazing pictures to share. I've used it many times over the past week, and it never gets old.
Creator Suite is a godsend for anyone making videos for social media, as it places the script right on screen for you to read while recording, plus additional tools that help with editing. Instant Night Sight is the perfect execution of a feature Google has excelled at for years, and the difference in capture speed in low-light situations compared to any other phone on the market is truly impressive.
Hearing the Pixel real-time translate someone's voice (and language) in a video into one I understand is magic. And while Rambler isn't a Pixel 11 exclusive feature, it's still the evolution of voice typing that many have wanted for years.
Now, while I had high hopes for HiLight, the feature is mostly useless. That glowing LED on the back lights up for phone calls, messages, and when you talk to Gemini, but that's it. There's no customization, making this an inferior version of Nothing's Glyph Interface. Likewise, Gemini Proactive Intelligence didn't seem to do anything of note for me, much like last year's Magic Cue feature.

One of the highlights of this release is a set of new cameras, all of which show notable improvements over the Pixel 10 Pro series. The main camera produces very fine detail, aided by Google's willingness to include grain in the image. I rather prefer this look, as it feels a bit like looking at film rather than an image from a digital sensor. That said, the colors are often too muted for my taste.
Telephoto performance is somewhat disappointing, but it has its highlights. While I can see some improvements over the Pixel 10 Pro's poor telephoto experience, it's still not as good as most Chinese phones' telephoto cameras (although it has a slight edge over the iPhone 17 Pro series). The new 120x zoom is surprisingly effective in some scenarios, though it's not something you'll use regularly.
Google also finally seems to have figured out how to make a food portrait mode, and I can happily report that the terrible artifacts and digital noise that appeared in Pixel portrait photos for the past several years are gone. Plus, the selfie camera no longer has that awful, compressed-image look that Pixel 10 Pro selfies suffered from, so overall, a very good camera upgrade year.
Should you buy it?
 ![The back of the olive green Google Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL next to each other](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/r5QL39VYdE5Bru5sjS6uGK.jpg) 
I can only genuinely recommend getting a Pixel 11 Pro or Pro XL for the Magic Capture feature. Google hasn't said anything about it coming to other Pixels, which makes sense given Tensor G6's improved TPU. Aside from this one amazing feature, however, the cost of these Pixels far outweighs the benefits.
But in addition to the downgrades, Google has simply given away too many Pixel-exclusive features to other phones (such as Gemini Automation and Rambler). I can't help but feel like it cheapens what the unique Pixel experience used to be. Maybe next year, Google.

title: Subnautica 2 Patch Adds Buddy System, Dev Reveals Glimpse at Early Access 2 Update
author: Wesley Yin-Poole
content:
Subnautica 2 gets its Buddy system update today, August 19. It adds a number of new features revolving around multiplayer in the underwater survival and crafting game.
In a new video, creative director Anthony Gallegos ran through everything players can expect from the co-op focused 1.2 update, which adds Proximity Chat, Player Trading and Revives, and an all-new Tracking Tag.
Gallegos said 1.2 includes developer Unknown Worlds’ first iteration of Subnautica 2 proximity chat. It includes an in-game voice chat option that you can use with your friends to talk locally with each other. As you get farther away it will switch to a radio-sounding voice that will progressively break up to a point where you can almost not hear your friend. “I think it definitely adds to the tension of it,” Gallegos said.
Also added is player emotes via a small menu that lets players cheer on their friends, clap, or tell them you’re a little annoyed or frustrated. Gallegos said he’s looking forward to seeing players use these emotes out of context to create fun moments, such as sarcastically clapping.
Inventory sharing lets players walk up behind another player, access their inventory and quickly swap items between one another, rather than having to drop inventory items out in the world and have them pick them up.
Player revives are also added, so if your friend is downed for whatever reason, you’ll have some time to share some oxygen with them and bring them back to life.
Two additional player characters (Grace and Jegna) are added alongside two new suit colors, “which should help with a little bit more of the diversification of players when you’re in multiplayer,” Gallegos explained. “You can still all look like the same character if you want — that’s something we support — but we like to have more options for you, and we will continue to roll out new options as we go through early access.”
Also included is the tracking tag, a short-range beacon you can throw out in the environment or put inside an inventory such as a portable locker, so if you ever leave it in a cave you can find your way back to it. If you die holding a tracking tag or have one in your inventory, it will extend your black box signal to help you find the stuff you left behind.
Improved HUD icons means all the icons will not be at full scale by default, but when you mouse over them after a half second or so they will scale up and give you the full details. “This is really nice because when you get really farther away from a region and you might have like six beacons, you turn and look at it, they're all really grouped together. But this allows you to more precisely pick the one that you want to know the information for without it feeling so busy on the HUD,” Gallegos said.
Alongside that, there are improved pinned recipes, which means the UI should feel a little less confusing, and improvements to the base builder tool that should help make it clearer when you can and can't build something.
Gallegos said this is just a chunk of the larger features added in 1.2, so expect more when the patch notes are available. Meanwhile, Unknown Worlds is continuing to work on the Early Access 2 update, which adds the new region, new story, new progression, new vehicles, and a lot more. The video showed a tantalizing glimpse at gameplay footage of this work-in-progress.
“The whole reason that we do make games at Unknown Worlds in this way is because we think we make the best games possible when you participate in this development alongside us,” Gallegos concluded. “And I think that this update shows that we really want to listen and prioritize the things that our fans are asking for.”
Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.
summary: Subnautica 2 released its co-op focused 1.2 Buddy system update on August 19, introducing multiplayer features like proximity chat, player trading, emotes, and revives. The update also brings two new character options, suit colors, tracking tags, HUD icon scaling improvements, and base builder tool updates. Additionally, developer Unknown Worlds previewed work on the upcoming Early Access 2 update, which will feature a new region, story, progression, and vehicles.

title: The iPhone 18 Pro Is Almost Here. These Are The Rumors We Think Are Real
author: Jibin Joseph
content:
![](https://sm.pcmag.com/t/pcmag_uk/news/t/the-iphone/the-iphone-18-pro-is-almost-here-these-are-the-rumors-we-thi_c7ed.1920.jpg) (Credit: PCMag/Apple)
We're reportedly only a few weeks away from Apple's next iPhone event, which is likely to include the launch of a foldable, as well as iPhone 18 Pros.
Customers usually hold off on iPhone purchases right before Apple’s fall event, but the RAM crisis and its associated price hikes may have you wondering whether it's best to buy now and avoid any more increases. Apple already raised prices across several major product lines in June, but the iPhone was not included, helping drive iPhone 17 sales during the last quarter.
To make your decision easier, we’ve rounded up the biggest iPhone 18 Pro rumors we have heard so far. While these features and prices aren’t confirmed yet, they should help paint a picture of what to expect from Apple’s next big smartphones.
iPhone 18 Pro: Revised Lineup
The biggest rumor around the iPhone 18 lineup is its release timeline. Unlike previous years, where Apple released four phones in the same series in one go, Bloomberg reports Apple could take a two-pronged approach to ensure consistent revenue throughout the year.
Flagship phones, such as the iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, and the first-ever foldable iPhone, could be unveiled in September, while the base iPhone 18, iPhone Air 2, and the iPhone 18e could be launched in spring 2027. We discuss the foldable iPhone in detail in a separate rumor round-up, so we’ll just stick to the Pro models here.
iPhone 18 Pro: Design and Colors
The iPhone 17 Pro models brought a major overhaul to Apple’s smartphone design language, with a new camera “plateau” and two-toned color scheme. This year, Apple isn’t expected to drastically change the device's appearance, but it could add a few bold colors and return to a more uniform color scheme on the back.
Several leakers, including Sonny Dickson and Instant Digital, claim that Apple could go with a never-before-seen cherry red and a new light blue, alongside the regular dark gray. Dickson also shared pictures of potential dummies, including one in light gray.
While the appearance of the rear is expected to remain the same, the in-hand feel could be a lot different. Ice Universe says the battery could get slightly larger on the iPhone 18 Pro Max, contributing to increased weight and bulk. More precisely, the leaker expects the device to be 0.25mm thicker and 7 grams heavier.
iPhone 18 Pro Display
On the front, we might see one significant change. The Dynamic Island, or the camera cutout, could be reduced by 35%, Ice Universe says. This won’t shrink the feature's overall functionality, but it could move the Face ID sensor’s illuminator to one corner below the screen.
When it comes to display sizes, the consensus is that the iPhone 18 Pro will come in its usual 6.3-inch screen, while the Pro Max will have a 6.9-inch screen. Apple, however, has reportedly been pushing suppliers to provide much brighter displays and could use the more power-efficient LTPO+ display tech.
iPhone 18 Pro Cameras
The iPhone 17 Pro lineup bumped all three cameras to 48MP. For the iPhone 18 Pro, the biggest camera-related rumor we have heard is around variable aperture. While the iPhone 17 models had a fixed aperture, the iPhone 18 Pro may introduce a variable aperture. ETNews reports that the modified system has already entered production and would help the cameras deliver more light to the sensors in dark conditions and reduce light in bright conditions.
Apple may also modify its relatively new Camera Control button. Introduced with the iPhone 16, the capacitive button at the bottom right of the phone lets you quickly launch the Camera app, take pictures, and adjust settings for zoom, exposure, depth, and other controls. Mastering the capacitive button, however, has proved difficult, with users noting that they have been accidentally launching the Camera app. Apple may finally fix the problem by removing the touch-sensitive components of the button and delivering a more user-friendly experience, 9to5Mac reports.
iPhone 18 Pro Performance
The iPhone 18 Pro is likely to receive a performance boost with the A20 chip. It will use TSMC’s 2nm technology, an upgrade from the previous generation’s 3nm tech. The transition will allow more transistors on each chip but also raise chip costs by 50%, MacRumors reports.
The chip is also rumored to have TSMC’s Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module (WMCM) technology, which infuses RAM into the same wafer as the CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine. Overall, it is expected to be 18% faster and 30% more power-efficient than than previous generations, according to leaker Fixed Focus Digital.
Apple usually reserves the base variant of its chip series for the standard iPhone models, while the Pro models get the corresponding Pro chip. With the iPhone 18 series, Apple is reportedly considering offering just the high-end variant across the lineup.
Another expected upgrade is for the modem. The iPhone 17 Pro models had an unspecified third-party modem, but the iPhone 18 Pro could get the company’s proprietary C2 modem. It will support 5G satellite connectivity and reduce the scope of location data retained by networks, according to MacRumors.
iPhone 18 Pro Battery
Apple never reveals its battery capacities, but multiple leakers have indicated a larger and more efficient battery for the iPhone 18 Pro Max. According to Digital Chat Station, the top variant will have a capacity of up to 5,200mAh, slightly better than the 5,088mAh capacity of its predecessor. With a more efficient modem and processor, the battery life could be significantly longer. The iPhone 18 Pro, on the other hand, could see a minimal bump from 4,252mAh to 4,288mAh.
More recently, leaks posted on Korean and Chinese social media sites tip a US iPhone 18 Pro Max model with a 5,567mAh battery, a nearly 10% increase over the iPhone 17 Pro Max, MacRumors notes.
iPhone 18 Pro: Pricing and Release
This is what much of the decision-making hinges on. Apple has avoided raising prices for its biggest revenue generator, but rising RAM and storage costs are unavoidable, by outgoing CEO Tim Cook’s own admission.
Common sense suggests a price hike for iPhones is inevitable in September. According to The Wall Street Journal's estimate, rising component costs would push the iPhone 18 Pro to start at $1,299. If you couple that with recent Apple trends, the iPhone 18 Pro Max could be priced $100 higher, taking its starting price to $1,399. In comparison, the iPhone 17 Pro starts at $1,099, while the 17 Pro Max starts at $1,199.
When asked on a recent earnings call about potential price hikes for the iPhone, Cook said it's "too early to come to a definitive conclusion of what happens there. Because it takes a little while for the channels to adjust since there's channel inventory, it takes a while for the consumer to respond. We'll understand that more in the weeks ahead."
The iPhone 18 Pro’s release date hasn’t been finalized yet. Going by previous event dates, Sept. 9, 2026, probably makes the most sense for the announcement, with a ship date the following week, but we'll have to wait for those invitations to hit our inboxes to know for sure.
summary: Apple's upcoming iPhone 18 Pro lineup is rumored to feature a split release schedule, new design colors, and a potential variable aperture camera system. Performance is expected to improve with a new A20 chip utilizing 2nm technology and a proprietary C2 modem. However, rising component costs may lead to higher starting prices of $1,299 for the iPhone 18 Pro and $1,399 for the Pro Max.
key_points: Apple may split the iPhone 18 release, launching Pro and foldable models in September and base models in spring 2027.
The Dynamic Island cutout could shrink by 35%, and the iPhone 18 Pro may introduce a variable aperture camera system.
Performance is expected to be boosted by a new A20 chip built on TSMC's 2nm technology.
Rising component and RAM costs are expected to drive starting prices up to $1,299 for the Pro and $1,399 for the Pro Max.

title: Gears of War: E-Day and Gibson Unite for a Custom Guitar Collection
author: Danielle Partis; XBOX Wire Editor
content:
As we count down to the launch of Gears of War: E-Day, Gibson Guitars and The Coalition are teaming up with a one-of-a-kind collaboration that brings together two legendary brands built on craftsmanship, authenticity, and storytelling.
The collaboration is a natural extension of Gears’ musical identity. Guitar-driven scores have helped define the franchise for nearly two decades, and Gears of War: E-Day composer Adam Lastiwka used Gibson guitars in the recording of the game’s soundtrack.
Inspired by the enduring brotherhood at the heart of Gears, the collection features two custom Gibson guitars based on the iconic Les Paul and SG designs. Created exclusively for Gears of War: E-Day, the guitars honor franchise heroes Marcus Fenix and Dominic Santiago through striking original artwork from acclaimed artist and illustrator Luke Preece.
“These guitars feel like the culmination of a years-long creative collaboration with Luke, who has been part of Gears of War: E-Day from the very beginning,” says Studio Brand Director Nicole Fawcette. “He loves Gears of War as much as we do, and he has a gift for translating the spirit of the franchise into striking art that makes you feel something.”
For artist Luke Preece, the project was a natural fit. “It brought together everything I love – music, metal, guitars, video games, art, and Gears of War,” he says. “All of those influences found their way into the guitars, so the collaboration felt completely natural.”
That sense of shared creative direction shaped the collaboration from the start. “Nicole and I had already established the visual language for E-Day, and we had a clear plan,” Preece adds. “We work well together and are usually on the same page, which gave us the freedom to focus on making the designs as strong as possible.”
![](https://xboxwire.thesourcemediaassets.com/sites/2/2026/08/Gears-Gibson-Spare-inline-164d65160610516cac79-1024x576.jpg)
Crafted for Brotherhood
Each guitar began as a hand-drawn concept before being digitally mapped, carefully stenciled, and meticulously hand-painted by Preece. Every detail was designed to capture the spirit of Gears through the lens of two of its most beloved characters.
The collection draws inspiration from two of the games “Emotional Core” pillars, Brutality and Pathos, ideas that reflect both the grit and sacrifice woven throughout the story of Gears of War: E-Day.
“What I love most about Luke’s work is his ability to communicate big, loud, bold ideas,” Fawcette says. “Rather than simply illustrating Marcus and Dom, we had the opportunity to distill their themes and energy into something iconic.”
![](https://xboxwire.thesourcemediaassets.com/sites/2/2026/08/Gears-Gibson-Marcus-LP-4d70589545554c8a51bd-1024x576.jpg)
Marcus Fenix | Brutality
Represented on Gibson’s legendary Les Paul, Marcus’ guitar embodies the grit, determination, and relentless spirit that have defined the character for nearly two decades.
At the center sits a weathered skull against a COG Tag backdrop, framed by the unmistakable blades of a chainsaw. Splashes of Locust blood and fractured textures evoke the chaos of Emergence Day and the world-shattering events that changed Sera forever. The result is a bold, aggressive design that celebrates one of gaming’s most iconic heroes while paying tribute to the franchise’s signature imagery.
“Marcus’ Les Paul was the hardest to solve. The hardware interrupted some of the original ideas, so we leaned into the circular saw-blade motif. It gave the piece the aggressive, brutal energy we wanted, and the shape fit the body of the guitar perfectly,” says Preece.
![](https://xboxwire.thesourcemediaassets.com/sites/2/2026/08/Gears-Gibson-Dom-SG-4fc8981bb05df225bb8c-1024x576.jpg)
Dominic Santiago | Pathos
Dominic Santiago’s design finds its home on the equally iconic Gibson SG, delivering a more somber and reflective counterpart.
A tearful, battle-worn skull stands against a COG Tag surrounded by barbed wire and vibrant crimson poppies, a powerful symbol of remembrance woven throughout Gears lore. The artwork reflects Dom’s unwavering loyalty, personal sacrifice, and the emotional weight carried by one of the franchise’s most beloved characters.
“Dom’s design came together more naturally through its symbolism,” says Preece. “The wings flowed beautifully with the shape of the SG and connected with the pathos of his story, including the angelic imagery associated with Maria.”
Together, the guitars tell a story of brotherhood, resilience, loss, and fate, themes that remain central to the world of Gears of War.
“Early on, we considered physically distressing the guitars to make them feel battle-worn,” says Fawcette. “In the end, I’m glad we preserved the beauty of the instruments and allowed the artwork itself to carry the weight and intensity.”
See the Guitars at Gamescom
“We can’t wait for fans to see these in-person,” says Fawcette. “Each guitar is already a beautiful object, and Luke’s hand-painted Gears artwork transforms it into something visually stunning – a genuine work of art that feels cool, heavy, and unmistakably Gears.”
Fans attending Gamescom 2026 in Cologne, Germany will be among the first to see the collection in person when they make their public debut at the XBOX booth.
Says Preece, “Only four guitars were made. Each is numbered and signed, and because they were painted by hand, even the repeated designs are not exact copies. Every instrument is a unique, one-of-one piece.”
Win a Piece of the Brotherhood
Starting today, fans can enter for a chance to win three custom guitars in total: two Marcus Fenix-inspired Les Pauls and one Dominic Santiago-inspired SG.
Fans in official XBOX supported regions can enter the giveaway starting today by leaving a comment tagging your Gears of War: E-Day companions and using #GearsofWarGibsonSweepstakes on the announcement post hosted on the @gibsonguitar and @gearsofwar Instagram accounts, for a chance to win one of the three guitars. The winners will be selected at random and announced on October 16, 2026. Check out the full rules, terms and conditions here.
Whether you’re a lifelong Gears fan, a collector of iconic instruments, or appreciate exceptional craftsmanship, the collaboration between Gibson and Gears of War: E-Day offers a rare opportunity to own a piece of Gears of War history as we prepare for Emergence Day.
Gears of War: E-Day launches October 6, 2026, on Xbox Series X|S, Xbox PC, Steam, and is available day one with Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.
summary: Gibson Guitars and The Coalition have partnered to create a limited-edition collection of custom guitars inspired by Gears of War: E-Day. Artist Luke Preece hand-painted four unique instruments honoring franchise heroes Marcus Fenix and Dominic Santiago. Fans attending Gamescom 2026 can view the guitars, and a sweepstakes is being held to give away three of the instruments.

The collection features two custom designs: a Marcus Fenix Les Paul representing brutality and a Dominic Santiago SG representing pathos.
Only four hand-painted, signed, and numbered guitars were created by artist Luke Preece.

title: 'Subnautica Began With a Love for the Ocean' — Subnautica 2 Dev Makes $100,000 Donation to Ocean Cleanup Charity as It Releases 1.2 Patch
author: Wesley Yin-Poole
content:
Subnautica 2 Early Access 1.2 is out now, adding the Buddy System to the underwater survival and crafting game.
Developer Unknown Worlds has also announced a $100,000 donation to the appropriately named ocean cleanup non-profit The Ocean Cleanup.
Unknown Worlds previously donated a portion of proceeds from the original Subnautica to The Ocean Cleanup on World Environment Day in 2019, and has continued to support ocean conservation efforts since.
“Subnautica began with a love for the ocean, and it means a great deal to continue the conservation work we started with the original game through this donation to The Ocean Cleanup,” said executive producer Fernando Melo. “We will keep doing our part to protect the ocean we have spent so long bringing to life.”
Unknown Worlds spoke about what to expect from Subnautica 1.2 yesterday, but today's release of the update brings with it detailed patch notes, below, which include a long list of changes and fixes.
1.2 includes the first iteration of Subnautica 2 proximity chat via an in-game voice chat option that you can use with your friends to talk locally with each other. As you get farther away it will switch to a radio-sounding voice that will progressively break up to a point where you can almost not hear your friend.
Also added is player emotes via a small menu that lets players cheer on their friends, clap, or tell them you’re a little annoyed or frustrated. Inventory sharing lets players walk up to another player, access their inventory and quickly swap items between one another, rather than having to drop inventory items out in the world and have them pick them up. Player revives are also added, so if your friend is downed for whatever reason, you’ll have some time to share some oxygen with them and bring them back to life.
Two additional player characters (Grace and Jegna) are added alongside two new suit colors. Also included is the tracking tag, a short-range beacon you can throw out in the environment or put inside an inventory such as a portable locker, so if you ever leave it in a cave you can find your way back to it. If you die holding a tracking tag or have one in your inventory, it will extend your black box signal to help you find the stuff you left behind.
Improved HUD icons means all the icons will not be at full scale by default, but when you mouse over them after a half second or so they will scale up and give you the full details. Alongside that, there are improved pinned recipes, which means the UI should feel a little less confusing, and improvements to the base builder tool that should help make it clearer when you can and can't build something.
The Subnautica 2 Early Access 1.2 update patch notes, courtesy of Steam, are below:

Gameplay

- Tracking Tag added to the game. Can be placed in carryables (like a locker) as a short-range beacon. If present in hand or inventory when reprinting, will increase black box range.
- Players can now revive each other before reprinting. Revived players will keep their equipment and regain a small amount of oxygen. Downed players can also choose to immediately reprint and respawn back at their assigned Biobed.
- Added Wave, Clap, Thumbs Up, Thumbs Down, and Frustrated emotes. Emotes are selectable from a new radial menu. Triggerable in water or on land, and can be interrupted by gameplay input.
- 🤿Players can now interact with each other to directly exchange inventory items.

- Adjusted Bulletheads so they deal more damage but can now be dodged (...sometimes).
